title: Scalar pasting propagates the unit orientation equation
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and put $h=gf$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Let $A_0\to A_1$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. In the ordinary pro-etale constant-ring derived categories and their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [det-sp-finite-general-ring], write $S_T=(-)\otimes^L_{A_0}A_1$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. For $i=0,1$ and $u=f,g,h$ put $G_{u,i}=u^!_{A_i}$, $H_{u,i}K=u^*_{A_i}K(d_u)[2d_u]$ and $\omega_{u,i}=G_{u,i}A_{i,\mathrm{target}(u)}$, where $d_f=d,d_g=e,d_h=d+e$. Use derived operations and twists [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $\gamma_{u,i}:H_{u,i}\simeq G_{u,i}$ be the diagonal purity family, $a_{u,i}:H_{u,i}A_i\simeq\omega_{u,i}$ its inverse orientation, and $t_{u,i}$ its tensor map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map, det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Write $c_i:G_{h,i}\simeq G_{f,i}G_{g,i}$ and $r_u:S G_{u,0}\simeq G_{u,1}S$ for the specified counit-normalized composition and exceptional coefficient maps [det-sp-composition-comparisons, det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Put $\rho_i=t_{f,i,\omega_{g,i}}$.

After the canonical scalar/pullback, twist and shift identifications, for every constructible finite-Tor $K$ over $A_0$ the scalar transport of the iterated purity map satisfies
$$G_{f,1}(r_g(K))\,r_f(G_{g,0}K)\,S\!\left(\gamma_{f,0}(G_{g,0}K)\circ H_{f,0}(\gamma_{g,0}(K))\right)
=\gamma_{f,1}(G_{g,1}SK)\circ H_{f,1}(\gamma_{g,1}(SK)).$$
If the unit equation
$$c_0(A_{0,Z})a_{h,0}=\rho_0(f^*a_{g,0}\otimes a_{f,0})$$
holds, then the direct diagonal orientations at $A_1$ satisfy
$$c_1(A_{1,Z})a_{h,1}=\rho_1(f^*a_{g,1}\otimes a_{f,1}).$$
All sources use the specified comparisons of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]; no flatness or finite projective dimension of $A_1$ over $A_0$ is assumed. In particular this implication applies to $A_0=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and any finite commutative $A_1$ killed by $\ell^r$.

source.place: proof (1), finite coefficient orientation identity: passage from prime-power coefficients to arbitrary admissible rings; former Step 8

proof.text: All arguments below lie in the stated categories. Apply [lem-sp-composite-projection-coefficients] at each $A_i$: $G_{g,i}K$ and $\omega_{g,i}$ are permitted inputs and the projections are natural, unital and associative. Its projections and counit-preserving compositor meet the hypotheses of [lem-sp-composite-tensor-transpose]. Consequently $t_{u,i,L}$ is natural in $L$ and $t_{u,i,1}$ is the unit identification; hence $\gamma_{u,i}(1)=a_{u,i}$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2), scalar extension preserves these constructible finite-Tor inputs without any flatness assumption.

source.place: proof (2) and final paragraph: domains and natural, unital tensor maps

proof.text:
Write $\lambda_{u,M}:S H_{u,0}M\simeq H_{u,1}SM$ for the canonical source comparison and $u_i:H_{h,i}1\simeq H_{f,i}H_{g,i}1$ for the twisted pullback compositor. Their source compatibility is
$$H_{f,1}(\lambda_{g,1})\lambda_{f,H_{g,0}1}S(u_0)=u_1\lambda_{h,1}.$$
Here every subscript $1$ used as an input denotes the coefficient unit, and $S1$ is identified with the new unit. For clarity this is the canonical tensor associativity square: after inverse image, each route sends a local tensor $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes y\otimes z b$. The ringed derived monoidal comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] compute pullback composition on K-flat complexes; the scalar/tensor and composition chain equations of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] give this equality before localization. All shifted Tate lines here are locally free and their scalar extensions are ordinary by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](3). Thus the same calculation applies to their positive tensor powers. The accumulated shifts are even, so their interchange has sign $+1$. This fixes the source identifications used below.

source.place: proof (1): canonical shifted Tate tensor splitting and its scalar identifications

proof.text:
Apply [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3) separately to $u=f,g,h$. In our notation its purity equation is
$$r_u(M)S(\gamma_{u,0}(M))=\gamma_{u,1}(SM)\lambda_{u,M}.$$
These are the direct diagonal/DNC purity maps over arbitrary finite rings, not newly chosen orientations: that normalization and the specified counit-characterized $r_u$ are explicit in the cited statement. Its hypotheses allow exactly $A_0\to A_1$ of the item.

Put $Q_i(K)=\gamma_{f,i}(G_{g,i}K)H_{f,i}(\gamma_{g,i}(K))$, $B_K=G_{f,1}(r_g(K))r_f(G_{g,0}K)$, and $A_K=H_{f,1}(\lambda_{g,K})\lambda_{f,H_{g,0}K}$. Successively use the square of Step 3 for $f$, naturality of $\gamma_{f,1}$ at $r_g(K)$, naturality of $\lambda_f$ at $\gamma_{g,0}(K)$, and the square for $g$. This gives
$$\begin{aligned}B_KS(Q_0(K))
&=G_{f,1}(r_g)\gamma_{f,1}(SG_{g,0}K)\lambda_{f,G_{g,0}K}S(H_{f,0}(\gamma_{g,0}(K)))\\
&=\gamma_{f,1}(G_{g,1}SK)H_{f,1}(r_g S(\gamma_{g,0}(K)))\lambda_{f,H_{g,0}K}\\
&=Q_1(SK)A_K.\end{aligned}$$
After the source identification $A_K$ this is the first displayed equality in the item. Naturality of $\gamma$ is part of [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3), and the source square used is precisely Step 3.

source.place: final paragraph: naturality, applied to the two coefficient purity squares

proof.text:
At $K=1$, Step 1 and the defining tensor expression for $\gamma$ in [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3) give
$$Q_i(1)u_i=t_{f,i,\omega_{g,i}}(1\otimes a_{f,i})(f^*a_{g,i}\otimes1)=\rho_i(f^*a_{g,i}\otimes a_{f,i}).$$
This is just functoriality of the tensor product, keeping the $g$-line before the $f$-line. The assumed unit equation is therefore $c_0(1)a_{h,0}=Q_0(1)u_0$. Apply $S$ to this equality and postcompose with $B_1$. By [det-sp-composition-comparisons](2), $B_1S(c_0(1))=c_1(S1)r_h(1)$, with these actual counit-normalized compositors. Step 3 at $(h,1)$ identifies $r_h(1)S(a_{h,0})=a_{h,1}\lambda_{h,1}$. Step 4 and the source equation in Step 2 identify the right side with $Q_1(1)u_1\lambda_{h,1}$. Cancel the isomorphism $\lambda_{h,1}$. Expanding $Q_1(1)u_1$ by the first equation gives exactly
$$c_1(1)a_{h,1}=\rho_1(f^*a_{g,1}\otimes a_{f,1}).$$
Only functors applied to an equality and cancellation of an isomorphism were used; no faithfulness of scalar extension is required. The map $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\to A_1$ is a particular unital map in the hypotheses, giving the final specialization.
